How to Unbox and Setup your Carvera Air

In this video, we’ll take you step by step through the unboxing process, showcasing everything that comes in the box: the CNC machine itself, accessories, assembly tools, and a materials. We’ll highlight the sleek design, robust build quality, and key features that make the Cavera Air stand out in the world of CNC machines. Whether you’re a professional or a hobbyist, this machine promises to elevate your projects to the next level.

In this video, we are guided through connecting to the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! Using the Carvera Controller App installed on a windows, mac, or tablet device, users can connect to the Air via USB or wifi. After connecting to our CNC, we can upload a Gcode file and begin to manufacturer our projects!

In this video, we are guided through uploading a GCode file to Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! After designing a part and preparing it in CAM software, you will need to upload the exported GCode file to the Carvera Air to begin manufacturing. This is done through the Carvera Controller app, as all files are stored on the Carvera Air's internal memory as shown in this tutorial.

In this video, we are guided through using the Quick Tool Change System on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The Air is equipped with a unique tool change system which allows for users to connect an easily swap the bit (also known as a cutting tool) on their CNC.
How to use the Wired Z Probe

In this video, we are guided through using the Wired Z Probe on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The Air is equipped with a wired Z probe which allows for users to measure and calibrate the height of the stock automatically. This not only makes setting up your projects easy, but also increases your machining precision too!

In this video, we demonstrate what the Auto Z Leveling feature can be used for on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The Air is equipped with a wired Z probe which allows for users to measure and calibrate the height of the stock automatically. But this wired probe can also measure multiple points on our stock, then adjust the machining depth based on the points recorded automatically!

In this video, we are guided through using the Dust Collection System on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The Air is equipped with a dust shoe and vacuum port which allows for users to connect an external vacuum to their CNC. This not only keeps the work area clean, but also creates a safer and more effective CNC environment.
How to Use the Air Assist

In this video, we are guided through using the Air Assist System on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The Air is equipped with an Air Assist system which allows for users to connect an external air compressor to their CNC. This can be used for chip evacuation and cooling when machining metals, or to reduce scorching when using the laser module.

In this video, we demonstrate how to unbox, install, and configure the optional 4th Axis Module for the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The 4th Axis with harmonic drive can be purchased as an accessory in the Makera Store, and this module can be installed on any Carvera Air. With the 4th axis, a wider range of designs and geometrically challenging parts can be manufactured in a wide range of materials. You can find the 4th axis for the Carvera Air in our store
How to Use the Laser Module

In this video, we look at how to use the optional Laser Engraver Module with the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera. The Laser Engraving Module adds a diode laser to the Carvera Air, opening up a wide range of projects and manufacturing processes on your desktop CNC. You can use this to cut and engrave a range of materials, like papers and fabrics, as well as for combined operations with the milling spindle like creating unique engravings or silkscreen layers on milled PCBs. And as shown in this tutorial, the laser engraving module can be installed quickly using the quick tool changer on the Air, just like any other bit!
How to use the Manual XYZ Probe

In this video, we are guided through using the Manual XYZ Probe on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! While the wired z probe is more commonly used, the Air is shipped with a manual XYZ probe that allows for users to measure and calibrate the height and position of the stock for a range of unique projects and circumstances. You would typically use the XYZ probe when mounting your stock in a fixture, or for aligning stock when machining multiple sides.

In this video, we are guided through connecting a Tablet Device to the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! The Air is equipped with universal phone and tablet mount that allows for users to connect an tablet device to their CNC. After installing the Carvera Controller App onto the tablet, this device can then be used to control the Carvera Air CNC!
How to Change the Spindle Collet

In this video, we are guided through changing the Spindle Collect on the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! Spindle Collet is the part of a CNC Spindle which that holds the bit. By changing the collet, you can change the diameter bit used for your CNC projects with the Carvera Air!

In this video, we are guided through updating the firmware for the Carvera Air Desktop CNC by Makera! Using the Carvera Controller App, we can check for firmware updates and update our CNC machines as updates become available. Firmware files can be downloaded for free from the software page on
The Carvera Air Desktop CNC machine is a complex electromechanical device full of sensors, electronics, and mechanical parts.
Parts do wear and faults are unavoidable during its long service.
Regular maintenance will reduce the wear and increase the life of the CNC machine.
Before starting any maintenance procedures ensure the machine is turned off and unplugged.
Vacuum or compressed air can be used for cleaning.

This case shows you how to use Carvera Air’s rotary axis to machine a 3D object. We don’t use dust collection for rotary axis machining, so we split the roughing and finishing process into two jobs. You should clean the dust between the two steps.
The Nefertiti sample model in this guide was from Thomas Roussel - Thingiverse: @lecaramel.
Note: Please read the instruction manual carefully to understand how to install and use the 4th axis.

Note：Some of the parameters for 4-axis and 3-axis machining are different: The 3-axis can be positioned using anchor point 1 or anchor point 2. The Y-axis position of the 4-axis is fixed, and the X-axis is positioned releative to the right edge of the headstock.
Note：We don’t use auto-leveling for 4-axis machining, and the auto z probe position is fixed.
Note：We don’t use dust collection for 4-axis machining. Please remove the dust shoe.

1. Plug in the cable and Install the rotary axis. （Please read the Carvera Air instruction manual for using the rotary axis）If your Carvera Air is on, please power off the machine first before installation.
2. Fix the Epoxy Tooling Board to the rotary axis, let the corner direction up and down.
3. Make sure the used milling bits are ready . No.1-3.175*25mm single flute spiral bit, No.2-30°0.2mmV-bit.
4. Turn on the power and wait for the automatic homing to complete.
5. Open the control software and connect to Carvera Air (please read Carvera Air instruction manual for detailed steps)
6. Open Root->Examples->Rotation in the remote directory.
2. Open the task configuration and operation dialog box.
3.  Set working coordinate to X offset 50 (relative to the right edge of the 4th axis headstock), and Y offset 0.
5. Check the “Auto Z Probe” option(4-axis z probe at fixed position, no configuration required).
